title: Why Blue States Can't Stop Minting Billionaires — TikTok
notes: Hook question: Democrats run against billionaires, so why do most new billionaires come from states Democrats fully control? Answer, scene by scene: wealth tax bills keep stalling in blue statehouses, opponents' arguments don't hold up in the data, billionaire money in politics flows to both parties, and a roaring market keeps minting more. The close turns to cities that act on their own (LA's Measure ULA, SF's Overpaid Executive Tax).

All figures are from the article (Jul 29, 2026) and the sources it cites (Citizens for Tax Justice, Political Email Archive, Pitchbook, Brennan Center, Americans for Tax Fairness, UBS). The news card is from Jun 30, 2026. California's billionaire tax was on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot; the script doesn't state an outcome.
VOICE: ElevenLabs, generated only after the author approves the script. Render drafts with --voice off.

post.headline: Why blue states keep minting billionaires
post.caption: Democrats have made taxing billionaires a core message, but 64% of the billionaires minted last year came from states Democrats fully control. Wealth tax bills keep stalling in their own statehouses, while cities like Los Angeles and San Francisco are acting on their own.
post.cta: Full story and interactive maps at the link in bio.

scenes.source: Why Blue States Can't Stop Minting Billionaires · American Inequality
say: America just had its biggest billionaire boom in 25 years.

scenes.source: Citizens for Tax Justice · American Inequality
say: At American Inequality, we found that 64% of new billionaires came from states fully controlled by Democrats.
Democrats keep promising to tax the rich, so we dug into why their own states can't do it.

scenes.source: Political Email Archive (Derek Willis) via Andrew Hall
say: In the first place, the party's message is all about taxing billionaires, which comes up in about 15% of Democratic fundraising emails.

scenes.title: Wealth tax bills in blue states
scenes.source: Why Blue States Can't Stop Minting Billionaires · American Inequality
say: The messaging is loud, but the bills keep stalling. Washington state's bill never passed because of constitutional limits, Illinois never got a vote, and New York's governor keeps resisting.

overlays.label: one-time tax on net worth over $1 billion

scenes.source: Why Blue States Can't Stop Minting Billionaires · American Inequality
say: California is now ground zero, with a one-time 5% tax on residents worth over $1 billion on the ballot.

scenes.source: Citizens for Tax Justice · American Inequality
say: California alone added 37 new billionaires in a single year, more than any other state.

scenes.title: Share of U.S. venture capital dollars, early 2026
say: Opponents of the bill warn that tech founders will flee, but California drew nearly 90% of U.S. venture capital dollars in early 2026.

scenes.source: Why Blue States Can't Stop Minting Billionaires · American Inequality
say: Governor Newsom says this fight belongs in DC, not with states, but history shows us that much of our progressive taxation has begun at the state level.

scenes.title: Billionaire spending in presidential elections
say: Money is part of it too. Billionaire spending on presidential races grew from $16 million in 2008 to $2.6 billion in 2024.

scenes.title: Super PAC and shell-group money in the 2024 race
say: Dems know who foots the bill. $1.2 billion of the outside money in the 2024 race went to Democrats.

scenes.source: Why Blue States Can't Stop Minting Billionaires · American Inequality
say: And a roaring stock market lifts the top 0.1% far faster than everyone else, giving this group even more power.
With statehouses stuck, the fight is moving to the local level, where progress still seems possible.

scenes.source: Why Blue States Can't Stop Minting Billionaires · American Inequality
say: For example, Los Angeles passed Measure ULA, a 4% tax on property sales above $5 million that funds renters and housing.

overlays.label: CEO pay over local workers' median that triggers the tax

scenes.source: Why Blue States Can't Stop Minting Billionaires · American Inequality
say: San Francisco also introduced a tax to ensure CEOs cannot make more than 100 times their local workers' median pay.
When cities lead, they prove the ultra-wealthy can pay into the places that made them rich.
You can read the full story on American Inequality.
